title: They Thought It Was Over… Until God Said, “I Will Restore What the Locusts Have Eaten”
paragraphs: They Thought It Was Over… Until God Said, “I Will Restore What the Locusts Have Eaten”
When everything feels stolen, wasted, or beyond repair—God speaks a promise that refuses to let your story end in loss.
There are seasons that don’t just hurt… they erase.
Not slowly. Not gently. But violently.

Dreams you nurtured—gone.
Years you invested—wasted.
Faith you tried to hold onto—shaken until it barely whispered your name back.
And the worst part?
No one really sees what was taken from you.
They only see what’s left.

Joel spoke into a moment like that—when an entire nation stood in the ruins of what once was. Crops devoured. Land stripped bare. Hope reduced to dust. The devastation wasn’t symbolic—it was real, visible, humiliating loss.
But what makes it even heavier is this: the locusts didn’t just take food… they took time.
And time is the one thing you can’t get back.
Yet right there, in the middle of devastation, God didn’t offer a coping mechanism.
He made a promise.

“וְשִׁלַּמְתִּי לָכֶם אֶת־הַשָּׁנִים אֲשֶׁר אָכַל הָאַרְבֶּה…”
“Veshillamti lakhem et-hashanim asher akhal ha’arbeh…”
“I will restore to you the years that the locust has eaten…” (Joel 2:25)

Not days.
Not moments.
Years.
Read that again.
God didn’t say, “I’ll help you move on.”
He said, “I will restore.”
The Hebrew word “שִׁלַּמְתִּי” (shillamti) carries the weight of repayment, compensation, making something whole again—as if the loss never had the final say.
Let that sink into the places you don’t talk about.
Because some of you aren’t just dealing with pain…
You’re grieving stolen years.

Years lost to addiction.
Years buried in sin.
Years wasted chasing things that left you empty.
Years spent in relationships that broke you instead of building you.
Years where you knew God… but ran anyway.
And now, quietly, you wonder…
“Did I miss my chance?”
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
But here’s the part that will shake you in the best way:
God’s restoration doesn’t follow human math.
He doesn’t need equal time to restore what was lost.
He compresses redemption into moments that rewrite entire timelines.
Look at Joseph—years of betrayal, slavery, prison… and suddenly, one moment before Pharaoh changed everything.
Look at David—from failure and scandal to being called “a man after God’s own heart.”
Look at Peter—denied Christ three times, then restored with three questions: “Do you love Me?”
God doesn’t erase your past.
He redeems it so deeply that it becomes part of your testimony.
The enemy wanted your story to end in shame.
God rewrites it into grace.

Even in the Greek, the heartbeat of restoration echoes in the New Testament. In Acts 3:21, the phrase “ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων” (apokatastaseōs pantōn) speaks of the “restoration of all things”—a divine resetting, a putting-back-into-order what was broken, scattered, and lost.
This is not partial healing.
This is divine restoration.
But there’s something most people skip over.
Before Joel 2:25 comes Joel 2:12:

“שׁוּבוּ עָדַי בְּכָל־לְבַבְכֶם”
“Shuvu adai b’khol levavkhem”
“Return to Me with all your heart…”
Restoration is promised…
But it is tied to returning.

Not halfway.
Not casually.
Not when it’s convenient.
With all your heart.
That means the hidden parts too.
The parts you’ve been pretending don’t matter.
The habits you’ve been defending.
The compromises you’ve been justifying.
God isn’t asking for perfection.
He’s asking for surrender.
Because the moment you truly return…
Restoration begins.
Not always instantly visible.
But undeniably real.
And suddenly, things start shifting.

Peace where anxiety lived.
Clarity where confusion ruled.
Purpose where emptiness echoed.
God starts rebuilding what you thought was permanently lost.
And not just restoring…
But multiplying.
Joel 2:24 says the threshing floors will overflow.
Overflow.
That means what’s coming isn’t just recovery.
It’s abundance.
This is where it gets uncomfortable for some people.
Because if God is restoring you…
Then your story isn’t just about you anymore.
It becomes a testimony.
And testimonies are meant to be shared.
Someone you know is silently grieving their “lost years.”
Someone scrolling right now is convinced it’s too late for them.
Someone close to you is carrying shame they’ve never spoken out loud.
Don’t keep this to yourself.
Because restoration spreads.
Hope multiplies when it’s shared.
And if this spoke to something deep in you…
Don’t just feel it.
Stay rooted in it.
Because supporting this mission isn’t about a transaction…
It’s about participation in spreading the Gospel.
If you truly want to glorify God…
Don’t just receive the message.
Help carry it.
Be honest…
Because the same God who spoke through Joel…
Is still speaking over your life.
And He is not done restoring you.
Not even close.
Even the years you’re ashamed to talk about are still within His reach.
And somehow, in a way only He can do…
He will make it beautiful again.
He doesn’t just give you back what you lost… He gives you a version of yourself that never could have existed without the breaking.
